items.content_html:
Summary

Updates the web extension data and some web platform data for Safari Technology Preview 257, and adds the message_serialization manifest key.

  • manifest.message_serialization: Chrome 148, Firefox not supported, Safari preview (https://webkit.org/b/330104). Chrome announced it in https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/whats-new.
  • runtime.MessageSender.windowId: Safari preview, with the impl_url kept (https://webkit.org/b/329185).
  • action.getPopup(), browserAction.getPopup() and pageAction.getPopup(): Safari is partial, because it returns the popup path as given instead of a full extension URL (https://webkit.org/b/329391). The fix is in Safari Technology Preview 257, so the partial entry ends at preview.
  • declarativeNetRequest.RuleAction.requestHeaders.header: Safari is partial, because it accepts only a fixed list of standard header names (https://webkit.org/b/290922). The partial entry ends at preview (Safari Technology Preview 257). The restriction applies from 16.4: w3c/webextensions#372 reports The header Sec-GPC is not recognized. in April 2023, and Chromium (a deny list, per that issue) and Firefox 113 accept custom header names.
  • Enums exposed on the browser.* namespaces in Safari Technology Preview 257 (https://webkit.org/b/329161): declarativeNetRequest.ResourceType, extension.ViewType, menus.ContextType and ItemType, runtime.OnInstalledReason, PlatformArch and PlatformOs, tabs.TabStatus and WindowType, and windows.CreateType, WindowState and WindowType. Safari accepted the values, but the enums were not exposed, so each supported entry gets a preview entry and a partial entry that ends at preview, like scripting.ExecutionWorld. The safari_ios entries that differ from Safari are partial with the same note, because there is no iOS preview. This is verified for the WebKit-based implementation (Safari 18.0 onward). The earlier 14 to 17 range follows the ExecutionWorld entries and is not checked. cookies.SameSiteStatus and declarativeNetRequest.UnsupportedRegexReason have no BCD entry, and every webRequest.ResourceType value is already false.
  • action.isEnabled() with a bare tab identifier (isEnabled.details_integer): Safari preview (w3c/webextensions#463).
  • AudioWorklet.port and AudioWorkletGlobalScope.port: Safari preview (https://webkit.org/b/299386).
  • WebGPU dual-source blending, the dual-source-blending feature and its use in GPUDevice.createRenderPipeline() and createRenderPipelineAsync(): Safari preview (https://webkit.org/b/329950).

Test results and supporting details

npm run lint -- webextensions passes.

  • https://webkit.org/blog/18652/release-notes-for-safari-technology-preview-257/

Related issues

Fixes #31192.

Fixes #31057. The icon_variants changes for Safari Technology Preview 257 are in #31072.

Summary

Adds a Safari note to css.properties.display.is_animatable: since Safari 27, display transitions are disabled for popovers and <dialog> elements. Support stays at 18 with no partial_implementation, as suggested in the issue, since WebKit disabled this on purpose while the spec questions are open. Safari on iOS inherits the note through mirror.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit bug 311648, "Disable display property transitions for popover & ", is resolved fixed by 310725@main on 2026-04-07, with the test LayoutTests/transitions/no-display-transition-top-layer.html. The commit cites w3c/csswg-drafts#13595 and w3c/csswg-drafts#13200. It landed while WebKit was at 625.1.14, which puts it in Safari 27 (625.1.29); Safari 26.6 shipped 624.4.5 and does not have it.

node lint/lint.js css/properties/display.json: all data passed linting.

Summary

Add a note to manifests.webapp.share_target that Chrome does not support Web Share Target on Linux. Edge picks up the note through mirroring.

This re-opens #30742, which I closed to stay within the three-open-PR limit.

Test results and supporting details

Chromium has no Web Share integration on Linux, since there is no native share system there (see Chromium issue 40542648, OS: Linux, status: New). The same bug is already cited for navigator.share.

As discussed in #29889, this is an operating system limitation, which falls under the exception in the "Operating system limitations imply partial_implementation" guideline, so this adds a note only, without partial_implementation.

npm run lint passes.

Related issues

Fixes #29889
items.title: share_target: Note lack of support on Linux for Chrome

items.content_html:
Summary

#20403 set Safari to 16 for these features. Safari 16's release notes do announce Web Inspector Extensions, but no Apple source names any of these APIs. Safari's extension APIs are defined in WebKit's IDL files, and none of these features appear there. Apple's documentation doesn't mention any of them either.

Test results and supporting details

devtools.panels: Button, ExtensionPanel.createStatusBarButton, openResource, setOpenResourceHandler, sources

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsPanels.idl L29–36: devtools.panels defines only create(), themeName and onThemeChanged. It has no openResource(), setOpenResourceHandler(), sources or Button.
  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsExtensionPanel.idl L29–34: ExtensionPanel defines only onShown and onHidden. It has no createStatusBarButton(), so Safari can't create a Button object.
  • A search of the WebKit repository finds no createStatusBarButton and no Button interface for devtools extensions.
  • WebInspectorExtensionController.js: Web Inspector's extension controller handles extension tabs (create, navigate, show, hide, evaluate script, reload). It has nothing for opening resources, a sources panel or status bar buttons.

devtools.inspectedWindow: Resource (and its getContent, setContent, url), getResources, onResourceAdded, onResourceContentCommitted

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindow.idl L37–44: inspectedWindow defines only eval(), reload() and tabId. It has no Resource type, no getResources() and no resource events.

devtools.inspectedWindow.eval() option scriptExecutionContext

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindow.idl L26–28: the eval options dictionary declares only frameURL.
  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindowCocoa.mm L48–56: the implementation accepts only frameURLKey. Other options are ignored. The same applies to contextSecurityOrigin and useContentScriptContext, which #31154 corrects.

Apple sources checked (none mention any of these features):

  • Safari release notes for 15.4, 16.0–16.5, 17.0 and 18.0. Safari 16.0 says only "Added support for Safari Web Inspector Extensions."
  • WebKit features in Safari 16.0
  • WWDC22 session 10100, "Create Safari Web Inspector Extensions". It names only devtools.panels.create, devtools.inspectedWindow.eval (with frameURL), devtools.network.onNavigated and the theme APIs.
  • Adding a web development tool to Safari Web Inspector
  • Assessing your Safari web extension's browser compatibility
items.title: devtools.panels Safari support corrections

items.content_html: WebKit treats -webkit-hyphenate-limit-lines as an alias of the unprefixed hyphenate-limit-lines property, so record it as a -webkit- prefix on hyphenate-limit-lines instead of a separate entry. It's also more helpful to have those as a combined entry so they both appear on the relevant MDN page later.
items.title: Merge -webkit-hyphenate-limit-lines into hyphenate-limit-lines

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds a gzip row to http.headers.Content-Encoding, next to br, dcb, dcz and zstd. Its data is the same as the Content-Encoding row itself.

I left deflate and compress out. IE only accepted raw deflate streams without the zlib wrapper, so deflate would need notes. compress doesn't work in any major browser.

Test results and supporting details

npm test passes. After npm run build, the resolved gzip support equals the parent row's.

Sources:

  • Chrome 1: Chromium's first public commit already decodes gzip and x-gzip (net/base/filter.cc).
  • Firefox 1: Gecko's HTTP compression converter handled gzip before Firefox 1.0 (nsHTTPCompressConv.cpp, June 2004), and the default network.http.accept-encoding was already gzip,deflate (all.js, October 2004).
  • Safari 1: WebKit loads through NSURLConnection, which came with Safari 1.0, and NSURLConnection decodes gzip and deflate (WebKit bug 4648, comment 6).
  • IE: decoded gzip in URLMon up to IE 6 and in WinINET from IE 7 (Compressing the Web, IEInternals). I kept the parent's ≤11.
  • Edge 12: Edge's first release, same as the parent row. Those first versions came from #23725, which covers headers in the HTTP/1.1 spec. gzip is a content coding in that same spec (RFC 2616 section 3.5).

Related issues

Fixes #31171
items.title: Add `Content-Encoding: gzip`

items.content_html:
Summary

Firefox lists readonly_and_readwrite_storage_textures, packed_4x8_integer_dot_product and pointer_composite_access in navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures, and has done so since WebGPU first shipped in Firefox 141. This sets those three to 141 with the same partial implementation notes as the parent WGSLLanguageFeatures entry.

Test results and supporting details

Firefox fills wgslLanguageFeatures from naga's ImplementedLanguageExtension::all() (wgpu_client_instance_get_wgsl_language_feature in gfx/wgpu_bindings/src/client.rs, called from dom/webgpu/Instance.cpp). At the FIREFOX_141_0_RELEASE tag, the vendored naga in third_party/rust/naga/src/front/wgsl/parse/directive/language_extension.rs lists exactly these three, and they're still there at every release tag up to 160.

The other keys stay as they are. naga added immediate_address_space in 154, but Firefox filters it out of the list until the rest of the immediates API is exposed (bug 2005059), and unrestricted_pointer_parameters is still in naga's unimplemented list.

I didn't run Firefox here, this is from the source at the release tags. npm test passes.

If #31176 lands first, I'll drop the service worker note from these three as well.

Related issues

Fixes #31175
items.title: Firefox 141 supports three WGSL language extensions

Summary

Updates the status of WebGPU optional features in Firefox:

  • The following features were listed as not supported, but were actually supported prior to the initial Firefox release with WebGPU support (141): depth-clip-control, depth32float-stencil8, texture-compression-bc, texture-compression-etc2, texture-compression-astc, timestamp-query, indirect-first-instance, shader-f16, rg11b10ufloat-renderable, bgra8unorm-storage, float32-filterable.
  • As a consequence of adding support in a second implementation, status.experimental changes to false for float32-filterable and texture-compression-bc.
  • dual-source-blending was already correctly reported as 155+; this PR adds the standard notes about platform limitations.
  • clip-distances, float32-blendable already correctly reported 158+.
  • texture-component-swizzle is in https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D343350 and can be added if this PR is still open when it lands.

Test results and supporting details

Ran npm test.

Related issues

Can generally be found via Bug 2073767 - [meta] Optional WebGPU features.

items.content_html:
Summary

Firefox supports WebGPU in service workers from version 148. Remove the note about the service worker restriction everywhere it appears. I have not replaced it with a note stating that support started in 148, to me that doesn't seem like an important enough point to be worth cluttering all of these pages with the note. But I can add it if desired.

There were two instances of the alternate note text "Supported on Windows only, in all contexts except for service workers." One of these was GPUDevice.importExternalTexture, where that note was correct when added, but is no longer correct. I removed it and replaced it with the full standard set of WebGPU notes (but support starts in Firefox 144, not Firefox 141).

The other instance was in the data for the GPUPipelineError message parameter being optional. I am not aware of any reason this differs from the rest of the WebGPU items, so I replaced it with the standard set of WebGPU notes.

I also deleted "Supported on Windows only, in all contexts except for service workers." from the OS_NOTES list in scripts/build/mirror.js.

CC @ErichDonGubler

Test results and supporting details

  • Ran npm test
  • Bug 1942431 - Remove Nightly gate on WebGPU in service workers
items.title: Firefox supports WebGPU in service workers from 148

items.content_html:
Summary

Safari 26.4 fixed devicePixelRatio so that page zoom changes it for the main frame. The data still marks every Safari version as partial with the "does not change when the page is zoomed" note, so this adds a full support statement for 26.4 and keeps the note for Safari 3 to 26.3.

Test results and supporting details

The Safari 26.4 release notes include "Fixed devicePixelRatio so that page zoom now affects the main frame consistently with iframes, keeping their values synchronized. (163857955)". That radar is WebKit/WebKit@bdfffc7361a6 (303397@main, bug 301807), which changes LocalFrame::frameScaleFactor() so page zoom applies to the main frame too. WebKit trunk was at 624.1.4 when it landed, Safari 26.3 shipped 623.2.7 and Safari 26.4 shipped 624.1.16.

A comment on bug 124862 reports the value changing with zoom in Safari 26.5, and #31039 has the same result in Safari 27.2.

Zooming still doesn't fire change on a (resolution: <n>dppx) media query (bug 317839), so the monitoring example on the MDN page doesn't work in Safari. That's about the media query rather than this property, so I left it out here.

Related issues

Fixes #31039
items.title: Safari 26.4 changes devicePixelRatio on page zoom

items.content_html:
Summary

Updates Intl.Locale and Intl.PluralRules compatibility data to reflect recent ECMA-402 specification changes needed by mdn/content#46518:

  1. Add javascript.builtins.Intl.Locale.firstDayOfWeek (Locale.json):
    • Chrome 128 (edge, opera, chrome_android, webview_android, samsunginternet_android, oculus mirrored)
    • Safari 18.2 (safari_ios, webview_ios mirrored)
    • Firefox 153 (firefox_android mirrored)
    • Node.js 23.0.0, Deno 1.46, Bun 1.1.22
  2. Record removal of javascript.builtins.Intl.Locale.getWeekInfo.returns_minimalDays_property (Locale.json):
    • Safari 26.4 (version_removed)
    • Deno 2.3.2 (version_removed)
    • Bun 1.3.6 (version_removed)
  3. Add options_notation_parameter and options_compactDisplay_parameter under javascript.builtins.Intl.PluralRules.PluralRules.options_parameter (PluralRules.json), and set deno to "1.8" on PluralRules.PluralRules.options_parameter to satisfy parent-child consistency checks:
    • options.notation: Chrome 143, Firefox 149, Safari 26, Node.js 26.0.0, Deno 2.6.7, Bun 1.2.16
    • options.compactDisplay: Chrome 143, Firefox 149, Safari 27, Node.js 26.0.0, Deno 2.6.7, Bun 1.4.0

Test results and supporting details

Primary source evidence verified against upstream engine repositories and release notes:

  • Intl.Locale.prototype.firstDayOfWeek:
    • V8/Chrome/Node/Deno: SimpleInstallGetter(..., factory->firstDayOfWeek_string(), Builtin::kLocalePrototypeFirstDayOfWeek, ...) is absent in V8 12.7-lkgr and added unconditionally in V8 12.8-lkgr (chrome 128). Node.js bootstrapper.cc lacks it in v22.21.0 (V8 12.4) and includes it in v23.0.0 (V8 12.9). Deno upgraded V8 from 12.7 (v1.45.5) to 12.9 in v1.46.0.
    • WebKit/Safari/Bun: WebKit bug 276943 (WebKit/WebKit#31103); absent in safari-7619.2.8-branch (Safari 18.1), present in safari-7620-branch / safari-7620.1.12-branch (Safari 18.2); absent in bun-v1.1.21 (f9a0fda2), present in bun-v1.1.22 (a060f087).
    • Firefox: Locale.cpp gated JS_PSG("firstDayOfWeek", ...) under #ifdef NIGHTLY_BUILD and javascript.options.experimental.intl_locale_info (false by default) in FIREFOX_152_0_RELEASE, and enabled/shipped it in FIREFOX_153_0_RELEASE (Mozilla bugs 1693576 and 2037069).
  • getWeekInfo().returns_minimalDays_property removals:
    • Safari 26.4: WebKit bug 302587 (WebKit/WebKit#54002, 303287@main), Safari 26.4 release notes, and verified removed in safari-7624.1.16-branch (IntlLocale.cpp).
    • Deno 2.3.2: V8 removed minimalDays in 13.6-lkgr; denoland/deno v2.3.1 used V8 crate 135.1.0 (13.5) and v2.3.2 upgraded to 137.1.0 (13.7).
    • Bun 1.3.6: oven-sh/bun bun-v1.3.5 WebKit 6d0f3aac0b included minimalDays, and bun-v1.3.6 WebKit 1d0216219a removed it.
  • Intl.PluralRules notation and compactDisplay:
    • V8/Chrome/Node/Deno: V8 commit 1ef70f2b18 implemented notation, compactDisplay, and conditional resolvedOptions output without a flag; absent in V8 14.2-lkgr, present in V8 14.3-lkgr (chrome 143). Deno v2.6.6 used V8 142.2.0 (14.2) and v2.6.7 upgraded to 145.0.0 (14.5). Node.js v25.9.0 used V8 14.1 (false) and v26.0.0 upgraded to V8 14.6 (true).
    • Firefox 149: Mozilla bug 1970162 (target_milestone: 149 Branch, duplicates 1991470 and 2003315); absent in FIREFOX_148_0_RELEASE and present in FIREFOX_149_0_RELEASE.
    • WebKit/Safari/Bun: notation landed in WebKit bug 293582 (WebKit/WebKit#45910, 295502@main), absent in safari-7621.2.5-branch (Safari 18.5) and bun-v1.2.15, present in safari-7622.1.22-branch (Safari 26) and bun-v1.2.16 (014cad89f5). compactDisplay (315426@main and WebKit bug 317534 / WebKit/WebKit#67543) is absent in safari-7624.4.5-branch (Safari 26.6) and bun-v1.3.14 (5488984d20), and present in safari-7625.1.29.10-branch (Safari 27) and bun-v1.4.0 (0f966e81b7).

items.content_html:
Summary

Chrome 157 adds support for the HTML-in-Canvas API; see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5172548013916160.

Most of the features of this API are represented in BCD already, but it was pointed out to me that SVG and MathML elements also take the global drawable attribute, so you can render SVG and MathML onto a canvas using HTML-in-Canvas.

This PR therefore adds data points for the drawable SVG and MathML global attributes.

I've also added data points for [HTML|SVG|MathML]Element.drawable, as I saw some evidence they exist, and logic suggests they should. However, on testing, they return undefined. I've asked the Chromium engineers for input on this (see mdn/content#46289 (comment)), as it seems like a bug to me.

I'll set this to draft status until I get an answer on this.

items.content_html:
Firefox ignores the no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin-when-cross-origin and unsafe-url referrer policies for cross-site requests, and uses the default policy instead. This was added in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1720294 and enabled by default in Firefox 100 in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826.

The current data marks these values as removed in Firefox 92. This changes them to a partial implementation from Firefox 100, for the referrerpolicy attribute of <a>, <area>, <iframe>, <img>, <link> and <script>, the matching referrerPolicy properties, and the Referrer-Policy HTTP header.

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • 92-99 only ignored the values in Nightly and early Beta: the pref was @IS_EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER@ until https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826 set it to true.
  • Same-site requests still use the values, so they aren't removed.
  • Cross-site top-level navigations still use them outside private browsing (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1734328, also Firefox 100), which matters for <a>, <area> and the header (which also covers links followed from the page).

The same fix for svg.elements.a is in #31151.

Again, this seems reasonable to me from the bugs, but I'm hoping maybe you have tests for this?

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46466
items.title: Firefox relaxed referrer policies: partial from 100, not removed in 92
